ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — History and Physical — Ella Fitzgerald — True-date frame: synthetic events are moved into the patient's historical lifetime. Codes, instruments, and treatments remain modern and are anachronistic.

code.originalText: New patient visit: diabetes with calf pain on walking, low glucose after late shows, eye and foot examinations, and cardiovascular risk

text.paragraph: New patient visit: diabetes with calf pain on walking, low glucose after late shows, eye and foot examinations, and cardiovascular risk [S]
This fictional modern episode addresses the presenting concerns below. [S]

list.item: Her calves cramp when she walks through airports and to the stage, and she is afraid of what that means for her legs. [S]
Her glucose has dropped low after late shows, once just before an encore. [S]
The vision in her right eye has blurred, and she worries about reading lyrics and set lists. [S]

text.paragraph: Historical basis. These claims are historical evidence, not findings from a modern examination.

list.item: Ella Jane Fitzgerald was born on April 25, 1917, in Newport News, Virginia, to Temperance and William Fitzgerald. Most biographies gave 1918, but her birth certificate and school records show 1917. [D]
In 1932 her mother died suddenly of a heart attack; orphaned at 15, she was placed in the Colored Orphan Asylum in Riverdale, New York. [D]

In 1934 she won an amateur contest at the Apollo Theater in Harlem, which brought her to the attention of the drummer and bandleader Chick Webb; she made her first recording with his band in 1935, and her 1938 swing version of the nursery rhyme "A-Tisket, A-Tasket" became her first hit. [D]

She won the Grammy Award for Best Jazz Individual Performance in 1958 for Ella Fitzgerald Sings the Duke Ellington Song Book, and received the Kennedy Center award for lifetime achievement in 1979. She was known as America's first lady of song. [D]
She began to have health problems during the 1970s; she had diabetes, which caused problems with her eyes. [D]
In the 1970s, after cataract surgery, she returned to touring more than 40 weeks a year. [D]
In 1986 she was admitted to intensive care for heart trouble and underwent quintuple-bypass heart surgery; the following year she was back onstage. [D]

text.paragraph: 6 later historical claims are omitted because they describe events after the index age. See the teaching note.
Historical biography with true dates. These events are not part of the synthetic care timeline.

list.item: Singer; back on stage since recovering from her heart surgery, touring in the United States and overseas, often two or three late shows a week with long travel days and meals at irregular times; performing is the center of her life [S]
Lives in her own home; a road manager and her musicians travel with her; a long-time dresser helps her prepare for shows. She decides who is told about her health [S]
Tobacco: does not smoke. Alcohol: rarely (AUDIT-C at the wellness visit). No other drugs [S]
Activity: stands for long sets on stage in heeled shoes; walks little off stage because of calf pain [S]

Access and equity: Medicare with a Part D plan and a supplemental plan; misses appointments when touring; reads standard print with difficulty because of her right eye. The clinic schedules around tour dates, uses video visits on the road, sends large-print instructions, checks drug costs before prescribing, and coordinates with clinics in tour cities [S]
Supports and strengths: her music, her audiences, her band and road manager, and decades of experience of her own body on the road [S]

tr.td: Type 2 diabetes mellitus with peripheral artery disease: cramping in both calves after about one and a half blocks of walking, worse on the right, easing within minutes of rest; no rest pain, wounds, or color change. Resting ankle-brachial index 0.62 right and 0.74 left, toe-brachial index 0.46 and 0.55; dorsalis pedis and posterior tibial pulses absent on the right and faint on the left. A1c 8.6% on metformin, glipizide and glargine, with low glucose readings (to 52 mg/dL) after late performances. Foot: protective sensation intact to the 10-g monofilament at all sites and to vibration; callus under the second metatarsal heads; hammer toes of the second and third toes; no ulcer (IWGDF risk category 2). Synthetic modern episode linked to her documented diabetes and its circulatory complications
S — Synthetic modern diagnosis; the type of diabetes was not made public and is synthetic.

Moderate nonproliferative diabetic retinopathy with center-involving diabetic macular edema in the right eye (best-corrected acuity 64 letters, about 20/50) and moderate nonproliferative retinopathy without macular edema in the left eye (81 letters); lens implants in both eyes from earlier cataract surgery. Synthetic modern episode linked to her documented diabetic eye problems
S — Synthetic modern eye diagnosis on retinal imaging and optical coherence tomography in the clinic; the left eye is described in the display.

Coronary artery disease after five-vessel coronary bypass surgery last year, with an intensive care stay; no angina now; on aspirin, a statin, and metoprolol. Synthetic modern episode linked to her documented heart surgery
S — Synthetic modern coding of her documented heart surgery; bypass grafts are described in the display.

Resting ankle-brachial index 0.62 right and 0.74 left, toe-brachial index 0.46 and 0.55; dorsalis pedis and posterior tibial pulses absent on the right and faint on the left. A1c 8.6% on metformin, glipizide and glargine, with low glucose readings (to 52 mg/dL) after late performances. Foot: protective sensation intact to the 10-g monofilament at all sites and to vibration; callus under the second metatarsal heads; hammer toes of the second and third toes; no ulcer (IWGDF risk category 2). Synthetic modern episode linked to her documented diabetes and its circulatory complications: active, confirmed [S]

Moderate nonproliferative diabetic retinopathy with center-involving diabetic macular edema in the right eye (best-corrected acuity 64 letters, about 20/50) and moderate nonproliferative retinopathy without macular edema in the left eye (81 letters); lens implants in both eyes from earlier cataract surgery. Synthetic modern episode linked to her documented diabetic eye problems: active, confirmed [S]

Coronary artery disease after five-vessel coronary bypass surgery last year, with an intensive care stay; no angina now; on aspirin, a statin, and metoprolol. Synthetic modern episode linked to her documented heart surgery: active, confirmed [S]

Comprehensive diabetic foot program: foot inspection, monofilament and vibration testing, and pulses at every visit; IWGDF risk category 2 with podiatry every three months for callus and nail care; protective daily shoes and low-heeled custom stage shoes; daily self-inspection with a magnifying mirror or her dresser's help; and same-day care for any blister, wound, or color change. Guideline: Standards of Care in Diabetes—2026 (2026); Practical guidelines on the prevention and management of diabetes-related foot disease (IWGDF 2023 update) (2023); CMID: Clinical Monitoring Intelligence Database, diabetes mellitus (type 2) and ischemic heart disease monographs (2026) [S]

Vascular surgery consultation for claudication with an ankle-brachial index of 0.62: arterial duplex, supervised exercise therapy, and whether and when revascularization should be considered, before any loss of tissue. Guideline: The intersocietal IWGDF, ESVS, SVS guidelines on peripheral artery disease in people with diabetes and a foot ulcer (2023); 2024 ACC/AHA/AACVPR/APMA/ABC/SCAI/SVM/SVN/SVS/SIR/VESS Guideline for the Management of Lower Extremity Peripheral Artery Disease (2024) [S]

Hypoglycemia safety on tour: glipizide stopped; glargine reduced 20% and moved to the morning, at a fixed clock time with written time-zone steps; a continuous glucose monitor with low alerts shared, with her consent, with her road manager; a glucose check before each show and a meal before late shows; glucose tablets in the dressing room and at the side of the stage; nasal glucagon with the road manager trained; and the beta-blocker's effect on warning signs explained. Guideline: Standards of Care in Diabetes—2026 (2026); CMID: Clinical Monitoring Intelligence Database, diabetes mellitus (type 2) and ischemic heart disease monographs (2026) [S]

Glucose-lowering medicines with heart and kidney benefit: empagliflozin 10 mg started, with sick-day rules (hold on days she cannot eat or drink and before surgery), genital hygiene advice, and a foot check at each visit; metformin continued with vitamin B12 checked; A1c every three months until at goal (goal below 7.5%). Guideline: Standards of Care in Diabetes—2026 (2026); CMID: Clinical Monitoring Intelligence Database, diabetes mellitus (type 2) and ischemic heart disease monographs (2026) [S]

Cardiovascular protection: atorvastatin raised to 80 mg with a lipid panel 4 to 12 weeks later and a goal LDL below 55 mg/dL; aspirin and metoprolol continued; blood pressure goal below 130/80 mmHg. Guideline: Standards of Care in Diabetes—2026 (2026); 2024 ACC/AHA/AACVPR/APMA/ABC/SCAI/SVM/SVN/SVS/SIR/VESS Guideline for the Management of Lower Extremity Peripheral Artery Disease (2024); 2023 AHA/ACC/ACCP/ASPC/NLA/PCNA Guideline for the Management of Patients With Chronic Coronary Disease (2023); CMID: Clinical Monitoring Intelligence Database, diabetes mellitus (type 2) and ischemic heart disease monographs (2026) [S]

Eye care: retina clinic appointment within two weeks for the right macular edema, for anti-VEGF injections; retinal examination of both eyes at least yearly and more often while being treated; large-print materials. Guideline: Standards of Care in Diabetes—2026 (2026); CMID: Clinical Monitoring Intelligence Database, diabetes mellitus (type 2) and ischemic heart disease monographs (2026) [S]

Kidney and laboratory monitoring: creatinine, eGFR and potassium at three months and then every six to twelve months, urine albumin-creatinine ratio yearly, liver tests after the statin change if symptoms, and vitamin B12 periodically on metformin. Guideline: Standards of Care in Diabetes—2026 (2026); CMID: Clinical Monitoring Intelligence Database, diabetes mellitus (type 2) and ischemic heart disease monographs (2026) [S]

Access and equity: scheduling around tour dates, video visits on the road, large-print instructions, drug-cost checks before prescribing, coordination with clinics in tour cities, and diabetes self-management education and medical nutrition therapy timed to her touring. Guideline: Standards of Care in Diabetes—2026 (2026); 2024 ACC/AHA/AACVPR/APMA/ABC/SCAI/SVM/SVN/SVS/SIR/VESS Guideline for the Management of Lower Extremity Peripheral Artery Disease (2024) [S]
Referral to vascular surgery, Marcus Okafor-Lane, MD, ordered 1987-05-11 [S]
